  "situation": "The coordinated estimates addressed the relationship between Moscow and Beijing. Earlier assessments recognized difficulties and significant differences but judged that the two sides would maintain their alliance and that conflicts were unlikely to impair its solidarity. Differences had become apparent over China's domestic programs, the Quemoy-Matsu crisis, and the implications of Soviet nuclear capabilities. In 1960, Moscow ordered its experts to leave China, and Chinese and Soviet spokesmen angrily confronted one another at international Communist gatherings.
